TEXT
The heading at the top reads "LUMINO".
The subheading below the heading on the left reads "INTRODUCTION".
The first paragraph under INTRODUCTION reads "Luminosite is the all-new, innovative navigation solution for the visually impaired. We hope that our app can be the all-in-one solution for our users."
The second paragraph under INTRODUCTION reads "Luminosite provides accurate, unambiguous instructions to the user via more intuitive means like haptic feedback for a much better navigation experience"
The third paragraph under INTRODUCTION reads "Luminosite integrates the use of the latest technology available like machine learning, augmented reality to provide our users with functionalities current solutions like cane and guidance dog cannot provide: contexting awaring surround cognition."
The fourth paragraph under INTRODUCTION reads "We hope this app can be a life changer for the visually impaired and revolutionize how people use navigation apps nowadays, creating a more harmonious, inclusive society for everyone."
The subheading below INTRODUCTION on the left reads "FEATURES".
The feature title on the left reads "Advanced Navigation and Guidance System".
The first paragraph under Advanced Navigation and Guidance System reads "Luminosite uses a more direct, intimate way of sensing - haptics. Accompanied by our custom-made navigation instruction algorithm, our haptic enabled guidance system can provide real-time, unambiguous instructions for our users to travel to their destination at ease."
The second paragraph under Advanced Navigation and Guidance System reads "In addition, we have incorporated the latest augmented reality technology - ARKit, to provide an extra layer of safety and accuracy to our users. Taking advantage of the dual camera on the iPhone 7 or later models, with ARKit, we can detect obstacles like walls in the 3D world. Besides, using kinematics information like the users' velocity and acceleration, we can provide warnings to the users in a timely manner and avoiding unwanted accidents."
The next feature title reads "Latest Machine Learning Technology".
The first paragraph under Latest Machine Learning Technology reads "Luminosite incorporates the use of machine learning to provide a more comprehensive experience for our users, in particular, machine vision and natural language processing. We use machine vision to help the users with visual disability to recognize a wide variety of daily objects in their daily lives. On top of that, we took a step further by providing the relative position of the object to the users, so that they not only know 'what' but also 'where' in front of them."
The second paragraph under Latest Machine Learning Technology reads "We also use natural language processing to allow users to operate the application via natural, fluent conversations, just like how we communicate with other humans. Natural language processing analyzes the users' speech as a whole, providing accurate analysis of the users' 'intent' even the user is speaking casually and not following any predefined format. This enables a smoother learning curve for our users as most of the functions in the app can be achieved by a voice command on top of a visual UI."

poster, LUMINO project poster

The heading at the top reads "LUMINO".
The section heading below the header at left reads "INTRODUCTION".
The first paragraph under INTRODUCTION reads "Luminosite is the all-new, innovative navigation solution for the visually impaired. We hope that our app can be the all-in-one solution for our users."
The second paragraph under INTRODUCTION reads "Luminosite provides accurate, unambiguous instructions to the user via more intuitive means like haptic feedback for a much better navigation experience"
The third paragraph under INTRODUCTION reads "Luminosite integrates the use of the latest technology available like machine learning, augmented reality to provide our users with functionalities current solutions like cane and guidance dog cannot provide: contexting awaring surround cognition."
The fourth paragraph under INTRODUCTION reads "We hope this app can be a life changer for the visually impaired and revolutionize how people use navigation apps nowadays, creating a more harmonious, inclusive society for everyone."

The section heading at left reads "FEATURES".
The subsection heading under FEATURES reads "Advanced Navigation and Guidance System".
The paragraph under "Advanced Navigation and Guidance System" reads "Luminosite uses a more direct, intimate way of sensing - haptics. Accompanied by our custom-made navigation instruction algorithm, our haptic enabled guidance system can provide real-time, unambiguous instructions for our users to travel to their destination at ease."
The next paragraph under that subsection reads "In addition, we have incorporated the latest augmented reality technology - ARKit, to provide an extra layer of safety and accuracy to our users. Taking advantage of the dual camera on the iPhone 7 or later models, with ARKit, we can detect obstacles like walls in the 3D world. Besides, using kinematics information like the users' velocity and acceleration, we can provide warnings to the users in a timely manner and avoiding unwanted accidents."

The subsection heading under FEATURES reads "Latest Machine Learning Technology".
The first paragraph under "Latest Machine Learning Technology" reads "Luminosite incorporates the use of machine learning to provide a more comprehensive experience for our users, in particular, machine vision and natural language processing. We use machine vision to help the users with visual disability to recognize a wide variety of daily objects in their daily lives. On top of that, we took a step further by providing the relative position of the object to the users, so that they not only know 'what' but also 'where' in front of them."
The second paragraph under that subsection reads "We also use natural language processing to allow users to operate the application via natural, fluent conversations, just like how we communicate with other humans. Natural language processing analyzes the users' speech as a whole, providing accurate analysis of the users' 'intent' even the user is speaking casually and not following any predefined format. This enables a smoother learning curve for our users as most of the functions in the app can be achieved by a voice command on top of a visual UI."

The application of UAV as a surveying tool allows geotechnical engineer to capture topographic data for landslide suspected site is relatively new. It is advantageous to adopt UAV technique to inaccessible natural terrains and unstable slopes which have repetitive failures. Those useful data would be extracted for further landslide analysis, particularly applicable for debris flow runout analysis which is sensitive to the topographic profile. poster, field trip poster for a Wun Yiu Village archaeological field trip titled "Innovative ways to automate archaeological work?"

The top line reads "The activity is supported by Tam Wing Fan Innovation Fund and Philomathia Foundation Innovation Fund."

The green rectangular logo at the top right reads "Innovation Academy Faculty of Engineering, HKU."

The yellow band near the centre above the main title reads "Field trip to Wun Yiu Village, the only Ming, Qing blue and white porcelain production site in Hong Kong."

The main title in the large yellow strip reads "Innovative ways to automate archaeological work?"

The left column body text reads "Did you know there was an ancient pottery-making industry in HK? Do you want to uncover the secrets of how families joined together to use local resources to make ceramics? Join us on an archaeological field trip to follow the clues of past human activity through the Tai Po River valley. Learn about the historic Wun Yiu temple, trek through banana fields and jungle to discover hidden artifacts of the past, see how animals were used to grind materials, explore deep into a cave rich in porcelain minerals... We will take you on a trip to the centuries-old Wun Yiu village to explore why almost half a million porcelain bowls were shipped from here across south Asia. Learn what archaeologists do, and see if you can contribute to studying the objects of the past. Archaeology is a field that has a low level of automation but needs more. During the trip, we will also think about how engineering can help archaeological fieldwork, such as through innovative ways to record and present archaeological sites and artefacts with new technologies. We will even play with an AR/VR app at the site. Let the adventure begin!"

poster, academic project poster titled "Identifying Priority Areas for the Improvement of Minibus Service Quality"

The heading at the top centre reads "Identifying Priority Areas for the Improvement of Minibus Service Quality".  
Top left reads "Supervisor: Dr. Ryan C.P. Wong".  
Top left below that reads "CIVL4102 Project - Tai Ho Ting Louis".  
Top right reads "The University of Hong Kong".  
Top right below that reads "Department of Civil Engineering".

The section heading at left reads "Introduction".  
The Introduction paragraph reads "The minibus is the third most popular form of transportation in Hong Kong, contributing 13% of all trips made in the city according to statistics provided by the Transport Department (2014). However, its popularity is still far from the more popular choices, namely rail and franchised bus which contribute 30% and 27% of all trips respectively according to the statistics. Despite that minibus is not the most important form of public transportation, it still has its significance as feeder service which connects local community to major transportation network. Therefore, this project aims to identify the priority areas for improvement of minibus services quality which could serve as a reference for related policy making in the future."

The subheading left reads "10 Service Aspects Concerned".  
The numbered list under "10 Service Aspects Concerned" reads "(1) Service hours", "(2) Route information", "(3) Waiting location", "(4) Waiting time", "(5) Ease of boarding", "(6) Vehicle stability", "(7) Safety", "(8) Reliability", "(9) Driver's service attitude", "(10) In-vehicle comfort".

The section heading at right reads "Data Collection".  
The Data Collection paragraph reads "The primary method for data collection is an on-street questionnaire survey conducted in December 2018 in Hong Kong. 6 student research assistants are kindly recruited by the Department of Civil Engineering of the University of Hong Kong to assist data collection. This survey is conducted primarily based on simple random sampling. The student research assistants approached potential respondents face-to-face and read the questions aloud. The final sample size of the survey is 547, in which 362 are for green minibuses and 185 are for red minibuses."

The section heading lower right reads "Ordered Logit Model".  
The Ordered Logit Model paragraph reads "The ordered logit model is adopted in this study to investigate the level of contribution of the 10 service aspects individually towards the overall satisfaction level. The model can be expressed in the following formulae."  
The formulae read "Yi = 1 if Yi* ≤ k1 (1)", "Yi = j if k_{j-1} < Yi* ≤ k_j (2)", "Yi = M if Yi* > k_{M-1} (3)", "Yi* = Σ_{k=1}^K β_k X_{ki} + ε_i (4)".

The section heading lower right reads "Importance-Satisfaction Analysis".  
The Importance-Satisfaction Analysis paragraph reads "The importance-satisfaction analysis is a key part in this study which aims to identify the priority areas for improvement by studying the combined effect of importance ratings and satisfaction ratings."

The figure caption below the left plot reads "Fig. 1 - Result of Importance-Satisfaction Analysis".

- the first paragraph in the Introduction reads "The world's fastest swimming robotic fish: a robot that aims to mimic the propulsive behaviour of real biological fishes, designed to swim in the complex dynamics of open waters. Our fish swims at low frequency of 4 Hz, a cruising speed of 2m/s with an input power of 150W, and can achieve high acceleration with a compact and compliant tail-like propulsor."
- the figure caption under the image in the Introduction reads "Fig 1. The robotic fish - latest design."
- the left middle box heading reads "Remote Control Implementation"
- the Remote Control Implementation text reads "The controls are implemented through the Raspberry Pi and Arduino, where the Arduino is used mainly for GPIO to send data to the Pi. A custom-built controller was designed using the FCC 220 433MHz RF receiver & transmitter (available with the Arduino). A custom communications mechanism sends power signals and turning signals to the fish. An auto timer is also implemented to prevent the controller from overflowing the buffer of the receiver. The orientation of the fish and fins is controlled using input from motion and orientation data, which is achieved with inertial measurement unit (IMU). The Pi utilizes its fast CPU to process the data, controlling servos with input from the camera while running machine learning (ML) models. The Sense HAT board, the Pi provides an accelerometer and gyro which maintain the orientation of the fish by a negative feedback loop and servo (fins) control. Upcoming work, we plan to perform system integration to connect the control systems and sensors of the robotic fish with computer vision components. We also aim to work towards deep reinforcement learning (Deep RL) for obstacle navigation."
- the small caption under the image in Remote Control Implementation reads "[unreadable]" (small caption partly unreadable)
- the center top box heading reads "Design & Manufacture"
- the first paragraph in Design & Manufacture reads "The latest version consists of about 250 individual components assembled together. The dimensions are 1250mm x 150mm x 520mm with a mass of 13 kg. - the second paragraph in Design & Manufacture reads "The materials used to manufacture the robot are PLA plus plastic, aluminium, rubber, and acrylic. Various manufacturing methods have been used including 3D printing, CNC machining, and traditional hand tooling methods such as cutting, drilling, sanding, soldering, etc. The electrical and electronic components such as the motor, encoder, batteries, Arduino, Raspberry Pi and the wirings are sealed in acrylic tubes."
- the third paragraph in Design & Manufacture reads "Several versions of the robotic fish were built. Each body differed in size and aerodynamic properties, with tails varying in shape, size, and material to try to achieve the best performance."

- the right middle box heading reads "Use Cases"

- the next subheading under Use Cases reads "Plastic Collection"

- the next subheading under Use Cases reads "Oil Spills"
- the paragraph under that subheading reads "Oil spills may take weeks or years to clean up. - the next subheading under Use Cases reads "Aquaculture"
- the paragraph under that subheading reads "To improve fishing and aquaculture processes, the robotic fish can use its speed and vision to survey the bottom of trawling nets. The fish can also serve as an ultrasonic robot to assist in the clean-up of biofouling (harmful buildup on fish nets)."
- the center-lower box heading reads "Factors Affecting Performance"
- the first subheading in that box reads "The relation between body length and fish swimming speed:"
- the paragraph under that subheading reads "For a motor with given power and the same tail design, an increase in length of the fish was found to cause less vibration during motion. - the next subheading reads "The influence of tail design and amplitude on fish swimming speed:"

1. WHAT IT IS
photograph of a memorial poster for Mr Tam Wing Fan

2. TEXT
- the heading at the top reads "In Loving Memory of Mr Tam Wing Fan".
- the subheading below the heading reads "FACULTY OF ENGINEERING / THE UNIVERSITY OF HONG KONG".
- the first paragraph of body text below the subheading reads "It is with profound sadness that we mourn the passing of Mr Edmund Tam Wing Fan (譚榮芬先生) on 12 May 2020."
- the second paragraph reads "Born and grown up in Hong Kong, Mr Tam was among the first cohort of Architecture students admitted to the Faculty of Engineering of The University of Hong Kong in 1950. At that time, the Department of Architecture was housed in the Engineering Faculty. After graduation, Mr Tam's vision, dedication, and enthusiasm continued to help him flourish in his architectural profession and business investments. He set up his own firm, the Edmund Wing-Fan Tam Architects. He became a member of the Hong Kong Institute of Architects in 1974, immediately after its formal establishment as an institute in 1972."
- the third paragraph reads "In addition to his professional vision, Mr Tam also served on the Board of Directors of the Tung Wah Group of Hospitals, during which time he advocated for the provision of much needed welfare services for the community, such as free medication, education, and dignified burial for the underprivileged, as well as relief for victims of natural disasters."
- the quotation paragraph reads "“Edmund always treasures his experience at HKU and it meant a lot to him. What he learnt from HKU, he carried all through his life. He very much wants the future generation of students to have the same privileges, and that is the reason why he wants to give back,” Mrs May Tam, his beloved wife, once said."
- the next paragraph reads "Mr Tam is proud to be an HKU alumnus and would like the next generations of students to be inspired in the same way that he had been during his studies at the University. In 2017, Mr and Mrs Tam announced their commitment to support the establishment of the Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing in the Faculty of Engineering, where students can expand their imagination and realize their ideas. More recently, Mr and Mrs Tam generously provided the Faculty with additional support to establish Phase II of the Innovation Wing, which focuses on high-level research to bring impact to society. His philanthropy also extended to the LKS Faculty of Medicine in HKU, other educational institutes, and non-profit organisations. In recognition of his contributions to society and the academic, The University of Hong Kong presented the Honorary University Fellowship to him in 2019."
- the final paragraph reads "We appreciate Mr Tam’s staunch support to the Faculty. We will remember Mr Tam as a warmhearted pioneer to foster the growth of future generations. We express our deepest condolences to Mrs May Tam, his family members, and friends."

While designing the robot, students are divided into 3 streams: mechanical, electronic and software. The mechanical stream is responsible for the design and manufacture of the robot's mechanical parts. The electronics stream designs the power system and circuitry used by the robot. We tuned the LLM on a dataset of 3D printing-related instructions and implemented a robust natural language processing system to accurately recognize and execute user commands, ensuring seamless interaction with the 3D printer.
Through rigorous testing and evaluation, we achieved impressive results with our LLM-powered chat-based UI for the 3D printer. The system accurately interpreted and executed a wide range of voice and keyboard commands, demonstrating its reliability and responsiveness. Users experienced a streamlined and intuitive control experience, enhancing their overall satisfaction and productivity.
Our project's successful implementation of a chat-based UI powered by LLM for 3D printers has significant implications. It revolutionizes the way users interact with 3D printers, simplifying the control process and making it accessible to a wider audience. This innovation has the potential to boost productivity, reduce user errors, and encourage further advancements in human-machine interaction within the 3D printing industry.

2. TEXT
- heading at the top centre reads "HKU iGEM 2023"
- large heading at the top centre reads "LEAPS"
- subheading under the large heading reads ""LOCAL ENVIRONMENT ALLIANCE""
- sub-subheading under that reads "PROJECT SERIES"
- section heading at upper left reads "# INTRODUCTION"
- paragraph under "# INTRODUCTION" reads "Hong Kong is a bustling metropolis with over 7 millions citizens. With its dense population and rapid economic growth, the city is facing a number of pressing environmental challenges that threaten the health of its citizens and the ecosystem. Given the versatility and precision of synthetic biology, it carries many potentials in dealing with environmental issues with high efficiency and small/no negative environmental impacts. "LEAPS" is a project series now consists of two subprojects, each tackling a different aspect of existing environmental challenges. With the achievement and success from the finished AMPed project, we now continue on our B-MAT system."
- section heading in the middle reads "# FINISHED SUBPROJECT: AMPed"
- paragraph under "# FINISHED SUBPROJECT: AMPed" reads "The project tackled the aquatic aspect of the local environment. The emphasis was on the Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) which is the phenomenon in which harmful microbes acquire genes resistant to antimicrobials. The effect of AMR has been observed in the local Pearl River Delta region. The fish industry is meanwhile heavily influenced by AMR as microscopic pests that infect fish can not be countered by conventional means."
- next paragraph under the same section reads "The solution provided is the transgenic AMP-expressing microalgae fish feed supplement that delivers passive immunity and nutrition to fish in aquo systems plagued with AMR. In the project, our team focused on the expression and production of Cecropin B (CecB) in the microalgal chassis Chlorella vulgaris var. autotrophica (Chlorella). CecB is an antimicrobial peptide(AMP) found in the Cecropia Moth (Echelobion Biosciences, 2022), with innate broadspectrum antimicrobial activities and no chronic of resistance. We introduced it to the food supplement as a fish feed supplement, and by designing two forms of products - the AMP isolate powder and the microalgal protein with the AMP encapsulated."
- next paragraph under the same section reads "The quality, mainly referring to the stability and toxicity, of the product was examined. The result is that not only CecB has high stability to pH and temperature but also it imposes no threats to health. Finally, the AMPed can be utilized by all farmers in the pisciculture industry and even amateur breeders with aquarium fishes."
- section heading lower left reads "# UPCOMING SUBPROJECT: B-MAT SYSTEM"
- subheading under that reads "Problem:"
- paragraph under "Problem:" reads "Battery recycling in Hong Kong has gained increasing attention during rapid industrial development. Currently, the two mainstream methods to recycle rechargeable batteries - hydrometallurgy and pyrometallurgy both come with negative environmental impacts. As an alternative, bioleaching is a recycling method that uses microbes to recover useful metals in batteries in a cost-effective and eco-friendly way. But current practice of bioleaching exhibits two main problems: (1) slow reaction kinetics, (2) Bacteria have low tolerance towards oxidative stress, hindering the scalability of the technology."
- subheading under that reads "Solution:"
- paragraph under "Solution:" reads "Hence, in this project, we propose a novel bioleaching system for lithium ion battery recycling using genetic engineered A. thioxidans. > We plan to: 1. design genetic circuit / overexpress genes (e.g. Sox, Hdr) 2. modify regulator in the A. thioxidans genome (e.g. MerR/MygA) 3. add Glutathione -> Metal resistance/ Anti-Oxidative Stress"
- next paragraph under the same section reads "Then the bioleaching process will be carried out in a two-stage method. (1)In the first bioreactor, our modified A. thioxidans will be cultured under suitable conditions. (2)The bacteria will be pumped to the second bioreactor to react with the wasted batteries. (3)After the bioleaching in the second bioreactor, our product is extracted through a valve and the recovery process is continued."
- subheading under that reads "Future plan:"
- paragraph under "Future plan:" reads "Apart from A.thioxidans, we are looking for other bacteria that possess similar function (e.g. A. Ferrooxidans) to further improve the leaching performance. And with a higher recovery rate and lower cost for battery recycling, we are considering extending the recycling to printed circuit boards or electronic wastes in Hong Kong. Since the components in these wastes are similar to batteries, bioleaching will also have a promising effect on their recycling."

photograph, poster showing a research poster titled "Trigger-specific Self-prevention and Preliminary Diagnosis of Depression using Flash Stimulus and GSR sensor"

the heading at the top reads "Trigger-specific Self-prevention and Preliminary Diagnosis"
the subheading directly below the heading reads "of Depression using Flash Stimulus and GSR sensor"
the line under the subheading reads "Presenter: Qi Baiqian Tong Anze  Supervisor: Dr. W.N. Lee (Ph.D., M.Phil., M.S., B.S.), Associate Professor"

the left column heading reads "Introduction"
the first paragraph in the left column reads "Depression is a common neurological disorder, from which 7.2% of people are estimated to suffer[1]. Meanwhile, different studies show that undiagnosed depression comprises a large share of all the cases, ranging from 40% to 75%[2]. This disease is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and the economic cost from an untreated patient can be up to 9950 USD[2, 3]. As the current pandemic puts people at a higher risk of getting depression, a better prevention and diagnosis solution is needed to avoid severe people and economic loss[4, 5]—the current technologies for prevention and diagnosis such as Questionnaires, Internet Behavioral Guidance, and Biomarkers Imaging, however, lack trigger-specific property. Meanwhile, finding the trigger and solving the problem or offering trigger-based psychotherapy is essential for treatment[6]. On the other hand, most of those technologies are clinical-based and are not available to ordinary people to raise their self-awareness of their mental health. The cost and stigmatization towards the psychologist have impeded people from approaching the professionals to prevent their symptoms from deterioration[7]. This study will discuss a breakthrough idea using flash-stimulus to find triggers and provide a possible solution to ordinary people for trigger-specific self-prevention and preliminary diagnosis using a GSR sensor."

the table row under "Prevention" reads "Current Shortcoming" then "Our Improvement"
the first cell under "Current Shortcoming" reads "Less distinguishing"

the second row under "Prevention" reads "No specific trigger" under "Current Shortcoming" and "Trigger-specific" under "Our Improvement"
the third row under "Prevention" shows "Clinical based - expensive" under "Current Shortcoming" and "Data based" under "Our Improvement"
the fourth row under "Prevention" shows "Complexity and accuracy" under "Current Shortcoming" and "Easy to use" under "Our Improvement"
the fifth row under "Prevention" shows "People's prejudice towards psychologist" under "Current Shortcoming" and "Self-operating diagnosis" under "Our Improvement"

the left column heading further down reads "Conclusion"
the conclusion paragraph reads "Globally, depression is a prevalent neurological disorder and can cause severe economic loss. Besides the direct burden on the health care system, the indirect cost on the undiagnosed patients are substantial[2]. Currently, the prevention and diagnosis technologies lack a way to raise self-awareness and provide trigger-specific solutions[5]. This lacking impedes people from preventing the depression deterioration or deterioration at an early stage, thus causing more severe people and economic loss. To break down their limitations, we propose a plan to give ordinary people a way to make trigger-specific self-prevention and preliminary diagnoses. Using the GSR sensor and the strategy of flash-stimulus, we provide a low-cost but user-friendly plan to help the users know better about their mental status. Similar experiments show that using flash-stimulus to find depression triggers is promising."

Poster: Eco.ly iGEM HKU 2021 A plastic degradation project.

The heading at the top reads "Eco.ly".
The small heading under the title reads "iGEM HKU 2021".
The large subheading under that reads "A plastic degradation project".
The left statistic heading reads "2000".
The left statistic body under "2000" reads "tonnes of plastic waste created daily in Hong Kong".
The centre statistic heading reads "79%".
The centre statistic body under "79%" reads "of PET ends up in landfills or is thrown away (PlasticsEurope, 2019)".
The right statistic heading reads "450".
The right statistic body under "450" reads "years in order for PET to fully break down (Armentrout, 2021)".
The section heading on the right reads "The Problem".
The paragraph under "The Problem" reads "Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is one of the most commonly used plastics worldwide. Cheap to produce, durable, and flexible; these properties make plastics ubiquitous and versatile in their use. Today, they are found in products ranging from food storage to textile to medical devices. However, the same properties that make plastics attractive also make it difficult to break down.".
The subheading under that reads "Current Solutions".
The paragraph under "Current Solutions" reads "Current methods of dealing with PET waste include dumping into landfills, incineration, and mechanical and chemical recycling. However, these efforts are not fully sustainable. Landfills require a lot of space, incineration release toxic gases such as methane in the process, and the different types of PET make chemically breaking down PET expensive. The newest recycling plant in Hong Kong, New Life Plastics, plans only to recycle specific types of PET.".
The paragraph continuing under "Current Solutions" reads "Decreasing plastic waste is a priority not only because we are running out of landfill space, but also because it impacts human health. Improperly managed waste can enter ecosystems where they interact with different organisms. Birds and fish can ingest or become tangled in plastic, where they suffocate, starve, or drown. 386 of 555 fish species surveyed by Savoca (2021) had ingested plastic. This means there is a high chance that we are also indirectly consuming plastics and the toxins they release. COVID-19 is only exacerbating the plastics waste issue as more eateries are using single-use takeout containers and utensils and using single-use plastic gloves.".
The section heading in the middle reads "Our Solution: Eco.ly".
The paragraph under "Our Solution: Eco.ly" reads "We create Eco.ly, a self-sustaining co-culture of the bacterium E. coli and cyanobacterium S. elongatus that can degrade PET. Genetically engineered S. elongatus are engineered to secrete sucrose across the cell membrane. The sucrose is taken up by E. coli - also genetically engineered, using it as an energy source to produce the enzymes PETase and MHETase. The PETase digests PET into MHET while MHETase further digests the MHET into terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG). The TPA and EG monomers can then be used for synthesis new PHA bioplastics via the genus Pseudomonas. Our system involves the design of three plasmids: the PETase and MHETase producing plasmid, the sucrose uptake plasmid for E. coli, and a sucrose secretion plasmid for S. elongatus. This system will be housed in hardware we have designed.".
A small schematic at left of the middle section shows an icon of a plastic bottle, an icon of a sun, and an icon representing TPA, EG with arrows and text "PET -> TPA, EG".
The left circular diagram heading reads "E. coli PET degrading plasmid".
The left circular diagram contains the readable label "PETase" and the readable label "MHETase".
The centre circular diagram heading reads "E. coli sucrose uptake plasmid".
The readable labels around the centre plasmid include "cscB", "cscK", and "cscA".
The right circular diagram heading reads "S. elongatus sucrose secretion plasmid".
The readable labels around the right plasmid include "lacI" and "cscB".
The lower section heading reads "Future Plans & Next Steps".
The paragraph under "Future Plans & Next Steps" reads "Much of our system remains to be experimentally tested. In the future, we plan on placing our system in our hardware to verify that the biological components will work as expected. We also hope to be able to more accurately quantify our system's PET degradation rates to identify areas of improvement. A mutant PETase-MHETase hybrid was recently shown to be six times faster at degrading PET compared to using PETase and MHETase separately (Knott, 2020). We hope to integrate these recent advances into our system.".
The continuation of the "Future Plans & Next Steps" paragraph reads "Additionally, we are looking to create new bioplastics using the Pseudomonas genus, where Pseudomonas naturally metabolises and accumulates PHA as a carbon and energy source to cope with their changing environment. The PHA can then be extracted and purified to create bioplastics.".

TEXT
- the heading at the top reads "The University of Hong Kong"
- the main title at the top center reads "INFLUENCE OF DISINFECTANTS ON MICROBIAL WATER TREATMENT PROCESSES"
- the byline under the title reads "By Chan Tsz Yui, BEng (CivE)"
- the supervisor line under the byline reads "Supervisor: Dr. G. V. A. Tan"
- the paragraph under the title reads "During the COVID-19 pandemic, the use of disinfectants has surged in order to contain the spread of the virus. Many disinfectants will be sent to wastewater treatment plants after use for treatment before discharging back to the environment. Nevertheless, studies have shown that large amount of disinfectants can inhibit biological reactions during the wastewater treatment process. The activated sludge process is particularly susceptible to disinfectants. Hence, this study aims to investigate the inhibitory effects of two common active ingredients of disinfectants, namely QACs and sodium hypochlorite, on the activated sludge process."
- the left column heading reads "Quaternary Ammonium Compounds (QACs)"
- the left column body reads "In general, QACs are considered as biodegradable in the activated sludge process since microorganisms in activated sludge utilize QACs as food and energy sources. Yet, studies have shown that high concentration of QACs can inhibit respiratory enzymes in activated sludge, causing activated sludge process to be interfered. Therefore, it is important to measure the percentage inhibition for each concentration of QACs to the activated sludge system."
- the schematic caption under the circular diagram reads "Schematic diagram showing how QACs inhibit respiratory enzymes in activated sludge"
- readable labels inside the circular schematic read "QACs" and "respiratory enzyme" and "Acetate" and "Acetyl-CoA" and "TCA cycle" and "ATP" and "NADH" and "Dehydrogenase"
- the right column heading reads "Sodium Hypochlorite"
- the right column body reads "Since sodium hypochlorite contains chlorine, it is sometimes added to activated sludge for chlorination and to control filamentous bulking problem. However, chlorination is not selective because it also affects COD removal rates and nitrification processes. Excessive sodium hypochlorite can affect the activities of activated sludge flocs. Therefore, it is necessary to define the concentration of sodium hypochlorite that leads to inhibition of the activated sludge process."
- the section heading below reads "METHODOLOGY"
- the left methodology panel text reads "Collect activated sludge samples from Sha Tin Sewage Treatment Works. To ensure that the samples have sufficient solids concentration, synthetic wastewater will be added to the samples before the experiment."
- the middle methodology panel text reads "Various doses of QACs and sodium hypochlorite will be added to the samples separately."
- the right methodology panel text reads "After six hours of retention time, the concentration of COD, NH4+, NO3- and NO2- will be measured to examine the percentage inhibition of the two disinfectants on the COD rates and nitrification processes."
- the section heading at the bottom reads "SIGNIFICANCE OF THE STUDY"
- the first bullet under significance reads "To raise public awareness of the ancillary environmental impacts of disinfectants"

To make the robot walk, it needs to control the motor underneath, and there are some obstacle avoidance sensors. The functions in ROS act like a bridge for the controlling programs of both motors and the sensors to communicate and coordinate.

- ----- A COMP3329 Course Project

- Introduction & Story
- FOOD City PANDA Run! is a 3D Runner Game developed during the course of COMP3329 Computer Game Design and Programming. The game idea is actually drawn from a book-keeping app called Fortune City which applies gamification of personal finance managing. We aim to apply a similar design to food delivery apps such as foodpanda, that the game can be embedded to those apps to meet business objectives as retain current customers and attract new ones.
  The background story goes as follows. In 20 AC (After Covid), Hong Kong is under a great depression of economy and food supply. To make ends meet, the player has to take a part-time job as a food delivery guy. However, in today's world, even the slightest mistake can lead people being fired, to make sure all the food reaches their customers intact, the player must avoid all obstacles appearing on their road of delivery...
- Technical Specifications and Assets Used
- FOOD City PANDA Run! is developed on Unity game engine and used c# as scripting language. All assets were purchased on unity asset store, including Hong Kong Street (for overall game scenes), Japanese School Lunch (for food choices), and Mobile Traffic System (for player car). For sound effect of the game, such as background music and coin collect effects, we referred to some online open source of audio materials. Some sample game scenes and assets are shown below:
- Player View of Roads, coins and Obstacles
- Player Car with Food
- Road Barrier as Obstacle
- Game Logic
  1. The player initially has 3 food on the tray for delivery.
  2. The player can move Left or Right by pressing ← and →, or A and D, to avoid hitting the obstacles and to collect coins as delivery tips.
  3. If the player have a minor or indirect collision (like pushing) with the obstacle, it will push the obstacle away without punishment.
  4. The food will drop from the tray if the player hit directly with the obstacle. The number of food that drops depends on how hard the player hit the obstacle.
  5. The player fails the game if there is no food left on the tray.

2. TEXT:
- Title: Weakly Supervised Localization for Assembly Line Understanding
- Supervisor: Prof. Wenping WANG
- Second Examiner: Dr. Jia PAN
- Jiarui WANG(3035332153) Yafei YANG(3035331501)
- FYP19015
- Headings: Background; Our Architecture; Experiment Result; Methodology; Data Set; Summary & Future work; References
- Background bullets: 1. Object Localization: Find where the object is and draw a bounding box around it. 2. Weakly Supervised Localization: Training data does not have localization guidance. 3. Our Task: Localize object being operated on assembly line in a weakly supervised manner.
- Our Architecture bullets: 1. Classification Sub-network Extracted deep feature from input image 2. Attention Proposal Sub-network Take in feature maps and generate parameters for image cropping. 3. Generate CAM: Map back weights from fully connected layer to the feature maps extracted.
- Methodology bullets: 1. Class Activation Map Visualize discriminative region used by classifier to make the prediction. • Different region is activated for different label prediction • Activation region is responsible for the corresponding prediction. 2. Recurrent Attention CNN Stack multiple CNNs to gradually focus on the most representative area. • Different classification network at different scale; • Additional module predict attended region to zoom in.
- Data Set bullets: label: Hard Drive, Power Supply and CD Rom • 7342 training images, 399 testing images
- Experiment Result bullets: For the baseline testing, we achieved 99.25% accuracy. For localization, we achieved 86.72% 0.25 recall rate. Apart from the base model, we evaluate the effect of data set processing, temporal loss, lr range and APN structure.
- Summary & Future work bullets: We implemented a new model with both CNN visualization and finer scale rescaling. we achieved 99.25% accuracy for classification, 86.72% 0.25 recall rate for localization. Implement APN with 3 stacked layers. Collect validation dataset and fine tune hyper-parameters. Compare with state-of-the-art's claimed accuracy.
- References: [1] Bolei Zhou, Aditya Khosla, Agata Lapedriza, Aude Oliva, and Antonio Torralba. Learning deep features for discriminative localization. 1. WHAT IT IS: Poster about an academic CIVL4102 Project on Microbially Induced Calcite Precipitation treated soils.

2. TEXT:
Title: Investigation of Influencing Factors On Engineering Properties of Microbially Induced Calcite Precipitation Treated Soils

Department of Civil Engineering
The University of Hong Kong
CIVL4102 Project
Timothy Ting
Supervisor: Dr. Man Man Hu

Background
- Soil improvement: modify and enhance soil’s engineering properties
- Conventional techniques: soil compaction, preloading, chemical grouting
- Chemical grouts may potentially damage the environment due to release of toxic chemicals (e.g. acrylamides) [1]
- Bio-grouting - Emerging Alternative: environmentally friendly, economical [1]
Microbially Induced Calcite Precipitation (MICP): A Promising Bio-grouting Technique

Bacteria and chemical solution (urea and calcium ions) injected into soil
Bacteria hydrolyze urea into carbonate ions [2]
CO(NH2)2 + 2H2O → 2NH4+ + CO32-
Calcite binds soil grains together, enhancing soil’s engineering properties
Carbonate ions combine with calcium ions to precipitate as calcite in soil pores [2]
Ca2+ + CO32- → CaCO3 (s)

Objectives and Methodology
- Investigate the effects of several influencing factors on the engineering properties of the MICP-treated silica sand
- Influencing factors:
  ⇨ Injected chemical concentration
  ⇨ Retention time of injection
  ⇨ Relative density
  ⇨ Sand particle size distribution
- Conduct laboratory tests to determine the unconfined compressive strength (UCS) and permeability of the MICP-treated sand

After MICP treatment:
- Calcite content determination
- Microscopic calcite precipitation patterns

Task List
- Sample preparation of a target size distribution
- Determination of max and min void ratios
- Investigation of effects of influencing factors
- Effect of calcite content on permeability & UCS

Expected Results
- Low chemical injection concentration → smaller crystals of uniform sizes precipitate evenly over sand particle surfaces, vice versa for higher concentrations [3]
- Increasing calcite precipitation → general decrease in permeability and increase in UCS [3]

Potential MICP Applications [2][4][5]
- Land reclamation
- Reduce ground settlement and soil erosion
- Resist against soil liquefaction
- Stabilize slopes and embankments
- Increase foundation bearing capacity

Image captions visible:
- Experimental setup for MICP treatment
- Pure silica sand before MICP treatment
- MICP-treated silica sand
- MICP-treated silica sand [6]
- Low chemical concentration [3] 200 µm
- High chemical concentration [3] 500 µm

Title: Weakly Supervised Localization for Assembly Line Understanding
Supervisor: Prof. Wenping WANG
Second Examiner: Dr. Jia PAN
Jiarui WANG(3035332153) Yafei YANG(3035331501)
FYP19015

Headings: Background; Our Architecture; Experiment; Methodology; Data Set; Summary & Future work; References

Background bullets: 1. Object Localization: Find where the object is and draw a bounding box around it. 2. Weakly Supervised Localization: Training data does not have localization guidance. 3. Our Task: Localize object being operated on assembly line in a weakly supervised manner.

Our Architecture bullets: 1. Classification Sub-network Extracted deep feature from input image. 2. Attention Proposal Sub-network Take in feature maps and generate parameters for image cropping. 3. Generate CAM: Map back weights from fully connected layer to the feature maps extracted.

Data Set: label: Hard Drive, Power Supply and CD Rom; 7342 training images, 399 testing images

Experiment bullets include: For the baseline testing, we achieved 99.25% accuracy. For localization, we achieved 86.72% 0.25 recall rate. Table and figure captions: Figure4. Statistics result for base model; Figure2: Overall Architecture of Model; Figure3. Example training data from three classes; Figure1. Class Activation Map for Different Class; Table 1. Summary of Experiment Result

Summary & Future work bullets include: We implemented a new model with both CNN visualization and finer scale rescaling. we achieved 99.25% accuracy for classification, 86.72% 0.25 recall rate for localization. Implement APN with 3 stacked layers. Collect validation dataset and fine tune hyper-parameters. Compare with state-of-the-art’s claimed accuracy

References: [1] Bolei Zhou, Aditya Khosla, Agata Lapedriza, Aude Oliva, and Antonio Torralba. Learning deep features for discriminative localization. - Body excerpt: "Firmware is the software program in MCU (micro controller unit) to control the actuators such as servos and motors, and sensors of a robot.
